display.title: Never Too Late to Repair: The Baal Shem Tov's Whisper
display.summary_short: On the way to a grandchild's chuppah, the Baal Shem Tov whispers to a passing stranger. His curious students learn the secret: a prank that turned into stealing, and a last chance to return the money.
display.summary_long: A week after Pesach Sheni, whose message is that it is never too late, the storyteller tells a Baal Shem Tov story from 'Talks and Tales'. On the way to a grandchild's chuppah, the Baal Shem Tov stops to whisper to an unknown wagon driver. His students, sure the man is a hidden tzaddik, find him at the inn, and he tells them his story. Visiting his best friend David, a peddler just back from a long trip, Moshe saw the sack of money David had earned left out in the open and hid it as a joke, to teach him to be careful. When David came home devastated, Moshe was too embarrassed to give it back in front of everyone. Day after day the yetzer hara talked him out of it, and finally persuaded him to invest the money far away and return it with profits. On that very journey the Baal Shem Tov whispered to him: return the money now; it is not too late, but later it might be. The children then share the lessons they learned.
display.lesson: Taking something without permission, even as a joke, is stealing; do not let embarrassment stop you from making it right, because it is never too late to do teshuvah.
